claim: Most transgenic crops are produced through tissue culture.
source_text: Most transgenic crops are produced through tissue culture.
evidence_reasoning: This statement reflects established knowledge about agricultural biotechnology practices.

claim: All tested regenerated rice plants had significant losses of methylation compared to non-regenerated plants.
source_text: We found that all tested regenerated plants had significant losses of methylation compared to non-regenerated plants.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is directly supported by the BS-seq experimental data presented in the manuscript comparing regenerated and non-regenerated plants.

claim: Loss of methylation was largely stable across generations.
source_text: Loss of methylation was largely stable across generations
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by experimental data analyzing T2, T4, and T6 generations showing 84% of sites that lost CG methylation in T2 did not recover in T4 and T6.

claim: Certain sites in the genome were particularly susceptible to loss of methylation.
source_text: certain sites in the genome were particularly susceptible to loss of methylation
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by the identification of specific DMRs that were enriched at particular genomic locations, especially gene promoters.

claim: Loss of methylation at promoters was associated with deregulated expression of protein-coding genes.
source_text: Loss of methylation at promoters was associated with deregulated expression of protein-coding genes.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by combined BS-seq and mRNA-seq data showing correlation between promoter hypomethylation and altered gene expression.

claim: Loss of methylation is stochastically induced at the tissue culture step.
source_text: Analyses of callus and untransformed plants regenerated from callus indicated that loss of methylation is stochastically induced at the tissue culture step.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by data from callus and untransformed regenerated plants showing different methylation profiles in individual plants from the same parent, and inferred from the pattern of variation observed.

claim: Changes in methylation may explain a component of somaclonal variation.
source_text: These changes in methylation may explain a component of somaclonal variation, a phenomenon in which plants derived from tissue culture manifest phenotypic variability.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the correlation between methylation changes and gene expression changes, and represents a speculative explanation for the observed phenomenon of somaclonal variation.

claim: Rice is one of the world's most important food crops.
source_text: Rice is one of the world's most important food crops
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about the global importance of rice as a staple crop.

claim: Tissue culture has been heavily used for decades for transformation procedures to generate transgenic crops such as rice and maize.
source_text: Tissue culture has been heavily used for decades for transformation procedures to generate transgenic crops such as rice and maize
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge in plant biotechnology, supported by the citation to Rao et al., 2009.

claim: Arabidopsis cell suspension culture has a different epigenomic profile compared to wild-type plants, with certain transposable elements becoming hypomethylated and certain genes becoming hypermethylated.
source_text: A previous study has reported that Arabidopsis cell suspension culture has a different epigenomic profile compared to wild-type plants, such that certain transposable elements (TEs) become hypomethylated and certain genes become hypermethylated
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citation to Tanurdzic et al., 2008.

claim: Changes in the epigenome have been proposed to be a source of somaclonal variation for decades.
source_text: Changes in the epigenome have been proposed to be a source of somaclonal variation (i.e., phenotypic variation among regenerated plants) for decades
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by multiple citations including Kaeppler and Phillips, 1993; Kaeppler et al., 2000; Thorpe, 2006; Rhee et al., 2010; Miguel and Marum, 2011; Neelakandan and Wang, 2012.

claim: The extent of methylation changes on a genome-wide level has not been previously assessed in regenerated plants.
source_text: However, the extent of methylation changes on a genome-wide level has not been previously assessed.
evidence_reasoning: This represents a gap in existing knowledge that the authors identify based on their review of the literature.

claim: Arabidopsis is almost exclusively transformed via Agrobacterium-mediated floral dip methods that do not utilize tissue culture.
source_text: Because, unlike most crops, Arabidopsis is almost exclusively transformed via Agrobacterium-mediated floral dip methods that do not utilize tissue culture
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge in plant transformation methodology, supported by citation to Clough and Bent, 1998.

claim: Arabidopsis is not a good model for the study of the effect of plant regeneration on the epigenome.
source_text: Arabidopsis is not a good model for the study of the effect of plant regeneration on the epigenome
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the fact that Arabidopsis transformation does not typically involve tissue culture, which is the process being studied.

claim: The rice genome is DNA methylated in all three cytosine contexts (CG, CHG, CHH).
source_text: The rice genome is DNA methylated in all three cytosine contexts (CG, CHG, CHH, where H=A, T, or C)
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations to Feng et al., 2010; Zemach et al., 2010.

claim: Rice has high levels of CG and CHG methylation and very low levels of CHH methylation.
source_text: with high levels of CG and CHG methylation and very low levels of CHH methylation
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations to Feng et al., 2010; Zemach et al., 2010.

claim: Whole genome bisulfite sequencing enables measurement of DNA methylation at single nucleotide resolution.
source_text: Whole genome bisulfite sequencing (BS-seq) enables measurement of DNA methylation at single nucleotide resolution
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about the BS-seq technique, supported by citations to Cokus et al., 2008; Lister et al., 2008.

claim: BS-seq allows one to distinguish DNA methylation in different cytosine contexts.
source_text: thus allows one to distinguish DNA methylation in different cytosine contexts
evidence_reasoning: This is a known capability of BS-seq methodology, supported by citations to Cokus et al., 2008; Lister et al., 2008.

claim: The tissue culture procedure induced stable changes in DNA methylation in regenerated plants.
source_text: We observed that the tissue culture procedure induced stable changes in DNA methylation in regenerated plants
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by BS-seq data from multiple regenerated lines and across generations.

claim: All regenerated lines had ectopic losses of DNA methylation.
source_text: such that all regenerated lines had ectopic losses of DNA methylation
evidence_reasoning: This is directly supported by the BS-seq data showing hypomethylation DMRs in all tested regenerated lines.

claim: Loss of DNA methylation occurred stochastically, affecting individual plants somewhat differently.
source_text: We found that loss of DNA methylation occurred stochastically, affecting individual plants somewhat differently
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by data showing different DMR patterns in individual plants regenerated from the same parent.

claim: Loss of DNA methylation was associated with loss of small RNAs.
source_text: was associated with loss of small RNAs
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by smRNA-seq data showing reduced small RNA levels at hypomethylated regions.

claim: Changes in methylation were enriched at promoters of genes.
source_text: changes were enriched at promoters of genes
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by statistical analysis showing significant enrichment of DMRs at gene promoters compared to randomized regions.

claim: Loss of DNA methylation at promoters was associated with altered expression of particular genes.
source_text: Loss of DNA methylation at promoters was associated with altered expression of particular genes.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by combined BS-seq and mRNA-seq data showing correlation between promoter hypomethylation and gene expression changes.

claim: An average genome coverage of 15× was obtained for BS-seq samples.
source_text: We obtained an average genome coverage of 15×
evidence_reasoning: This is a direct measurement from the sequencing data as reported in Table 1.

claim: Error rates for BS-seq were low at 1.5%, 1.2%, 0.8%, for CG, CHG, CHH methylation, respectively.
source_text: error rates were low at 1.5%, 1.2%, 0.8%, for CG, CHG, CHH methylation, respectively
evidence_reasoning: These error rates were calculated from the chloroplast genome methylation levels in the BS-seq data.

claim: 84% of sites that lost CG methylation in the T2 generation did not recover methylation in the T4 and T6 generations.
source_text: 84% of sites that lost CG methylation in the T2 did not recover methylation in the T4 and T6 generations
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative result from analyzing methylation status across generations in samples 4, 6, and 8.

claim: Loss of DNA methylation in regenerated plants occurred in non-CG contexts.
source_text: Loss of DNA methylation in regenerated plants also occurred in non-CG contexts
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by identification of CHG and CHH hypomethylation DMRs in the BS-seq data.

claim: The most significant enrichments of DMRs were at the promoters of genes.
source_text: we found the most significant enrichments of DMRs at the promoters of genes
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by statistical analysis comparing observed DMR overlap with gene promoters versus randomized regions.

claim: Loss of DNA methylation at promoters was associated with higher expression levels of certain genes.
source_text: We found that loss of DNA methylation at promoters was associated with higher expression levels of certain genes
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by mRNA-seq data showing increased expression of genes with promoter hypomethylation.

claim: The closer the hypomethylation was to the gene transcription start site, the more likely the gene tended to be misregulated.
source_text: Notably, the closer the hypomethylation was to the gene transcription start site, the more likely the gene tended to be misregulated
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by analysis of DMR distance from TSS and correlation with gene expression changes.

claim: The expression of genes with promoter hypomethylation was much more frequently increased, rather than decreased.
source_text: Furthermore, the expression of these genes was much more frequently increased, rather than decreased
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by mRNA-seq data showing directional bias toward upregulation in genes with promoter hypomethylation.

claim: The misexpression of genes with promoter hypomethylation is likely a direct consequence of losses of DNA methylation.
source_text: suggesting that the misexpression of these genes is likely a direct consequence of losses of DNA methylation
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the correlation between hypomethylation and increased expression, and the directional bias of the effect.

claim: Loss of DNA methylation in regenerated plants is associated with deregulated transcription of certain protein-coding genes.
source_text: Hence loss of DNA methylation in regenerated plants is associated with deregulated transcription of certain protein-coding genes.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by combined BS-seq and mRNA-seq data showing correlation between methylation loss and expression changes.

claim: Each regenerated plant has distinct DNA methylation profiles despite coming from the same parent.
source_text: Our results suggest that each regenerated plant has distinct DNA methylation profiles despite coming from the same parent
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by BS-seq data from three individual plants regenerated from the same parent showing different DMR patterns.

claim: The tissue culture step induces DNA hypomethylation in a stochastic manner affecting individual plants differently.
source_text: It therefore appears that the tissue culture step induces DNA hypomethylation in a rather stochastic manner affecting individual plants differently.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the observation that individual plants from the same parent have different methylation profiles after tissue culture.

claim: Descendants of regenerated plants stably maintain most hypomethylation across plant generations.
source_text: We further show that descendants of regenerated plants stably maintain most hypomethylation across plant generations
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by data showing 84% of hypomethylation sites remain unmethylated across T2, T4, and T6 generations.

claim: Lines derived from the same original regenerated plant show very similar methylation profiles.
source_text: Indeed, lines derived from the same original regenerated plant show very similar methylation profiles
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by hierarchical clustering and overlap analysis of DMRs showing high similarity between samples 4-8 and 11-12.

claim: Stochastic hypomethylation in individual regenerants is associated with misregulated expression of certain genes.
source_text: Our genome-wide data support this notion since we show that stochastic hypomethylation in individual regenerants is associated with misregulated expression of certain genes.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by combined BS-seq and mRNA-seq data showing correlation between hypomethylation and gene expression changes.

claim: Epigenetic changes likely explain a component of somaclonal variation.
source_text: These epigenetic changes likely explain a component of somaclonal variation that has been observed for decades in a number of plant species.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the correlation between stochastic methylation changes and gene expression changes, combined with knowledge of somaclonal variation.

claim: Use of tissue culture leaves behind an epigenetic footprint in regenerated plants that is stable over multiple generations.
source_text: In summary, our results suggest that use of tissue culture leaves behind an epigenetic footprint in regenerated plants that is stable over multiple generations
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by BS-seq data showing persistent hypomethylation across T2, T4, and T6 generations.

claim: The epigenetic footprint from tissue culture may partially explain somaclonal variation.
source_text: may partially explain somaclonal variation
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the correlation between methylation changes and gene expression changes, representing a speculative explanation for somaclonal variation.

claim: A common practice in agricultural biotechnology is to introgress new transgene loci into commercial genetic backgrounds.
source_text: a common practice in the development of agricultural biotechnology traits is to introgress new transgene loci into commercial genetic backgrounds
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge in agricultural biotechnology, supported by citations to Bregitzer et al., 2008; Bennetzen and Hake, 2009; Johnson, 2009; Yang et al., 2012.

claim: Plants used in agriculture are many generations removed from the initial regenerated plants.
source_text: meaning that the plants used in agriculture are many generations removed from the initial regenerated plants
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about agricultural breeding practices, supported by citations to Bregitzer et al., 2008; Bennetzen and Hake, 2009; Johnson, 2009; Yang et al., 2012.

claim: The crosses utilized in introgression schemes are likely to correct the vast majority of tissue culture-induced epigenetic changes.
source_text: The crosses utilized in these introgression schemes are likely to correct the vast majority of tissue culture-induced epigenetic changes.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative inference based on the understanding that crossing and multiple generations of breeding would dilute or correct epigenetic changes.

claim: Certain genes are hypermethylated in Arabidopsis cell suspension culture and callus.
source_text: Previous reports have indicated that certain genes are hypermethylated in Arabidopsis cell suspension culture and callus
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations to previous studies on Arabidopsis cell culture.

claim: Hypermethylation in rice callus predominantly occurs in CHH sequence contexts.
source_text: We extend this observation by showing that hypermethylation predominantly occurs in CHH sequence contexts
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by BS-seq data from callus samples showing CHH hypermethylation DMRs.

claim: CHH hypermethylation in callus occurs most notably at the promoters of genes.
source_text: most notably occurring at the promoters of genes
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by analysis showing enrichment of CHH hypermethylation DMRs at gene promoters in callus samples.

claim: CHH hypermethylation was completely eliminated upon regeneration.
source_text: we found that this CHH hypermethylation was completely eliminated upon regeneration
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by BS-seq data comparing callus and regenerated plants showing loss of CHH hypermethylation after regeneration.

claim: CHH hypermethylation may be linked specifically to the dedifferentiated state.
source_text: suggesting that CHH hypermethylation may be linked specifically to the dedifferentiated state
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the observation that CHH hypermethylation is present in callus but eliminated upon regeneration, representing a speculative interpretation.

claim: Global hypomethylation at TEs was not observed in rice callus.
source_text: In contrast to Arabidopsis cell culture, we did not observe global hypomethylation at TEs in rice callus.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by BS-seq data from rice callus samples showing no widespread TE hypomethylation.

claim: DNA methylation was specifically lost at certain sites in the genome in rice callus.
source_text: Instead, we found that DNA methylation was specifically lost at certain sites in the genome
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by identification of specific hypomethylation DMRs in callus BS-seq data.

claim: Loss of DNA methylation was maintained upon plant regeneration.
source_text: We found that loss of DNA methylation was maintained upon plant regeneration
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by BS-seq data comparing callus and regenerated plants showing persistence of hypomethylation.

claim: Loss of DNA methylation occurred in all sequence contexts.
source_text: Loss of DNA methylation occurred in all sequence contexts
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by identification of CG, CHG, and CHH hypomethylation DMRs in the BS-seq data.

claim: Loss of DNA methylation was associated with loss of 24-nt siRNAs.
source_text: and was associated with loss of 24-nt siRNAs
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by smRNA-seq data showing reduced 24-nt siRNA levels at hypomethylated regions.

claim: Hypomethylation sites were frequently associated with promoters of genes.
source_text: Notably, these sites were frequently associated with promoters of genes
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by statistical analysis showing enrichment of DMRs at gene promoters.

claim: Loss of DNA methylation was associated with misregulation of expression of proximal protein-coding genes.
source_text: and loss of DNA methylation was associated with misregulation of expression of proximal protein-coding genes
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by combined BS-seq and mRNA-seq data showing correlation between hypomethylation and expression changes.

claim: Genes significantly up-regulated in each regenerated line were somewhat different.
source_text: Interestingly, genes significantly up-regulated (fourfold upregulated compared to wild type, p<0.01) in each regenerated line were somewhat different
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by mRNA-seq data showing different sets of upregulated genes across different regenerated lines.

claim: It is difficult to assess the severity of impact of misregulated gene expression for any particular regenerated line.
source_text: For this reason, it is difficult to assess the severity of impact of misregulated gene expression for any particular regenerated line
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the observation that different genes are affected in different lines, making it hard to predict biological impact.

claim: Some regenerated lines may have more biologically important genes affected than others.
source_text: since some lines may have more biologically important genes affected than others
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative inference based on the variable nature of which genes are affected in different lines.

claim: Somoclonal variation affects only a proportion of plants that arise from regeneration experiments.
source_text: This would correlate with the observation that somoclonal variation affects only a proportion of plants that arise from regeneration experiments
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about somaclonal variation, supported by citations to Kaeppler and Phillips, 1993; Kaeppler et al., 2000; Thorpe, 2006; Rhee et al., 2010; Miguel and Marum, 2011; Neelakandan and Wang, 2012.

claim: Certain TEs such as Tos17 and mPing are reactivated in tissue culture and are associated with changes in DNA methylation.
source_text: Previous studies have shown that certain TEs such as Tos17 and mPing are reactivated in tissue culture, and are associated with changes in DNA methylation
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to Neelakandan and Wang, 2012.

claim: Most DNA hypomethylation occurs near genes and is relatively depleted at TE related sequences.
source_text: While our results suggest that most DNA hypomethylation occurs near genes and are relatively depleted at TE related sequences
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by analysis showing enrichment of DMRs at gene promoters and relative depletion at TEs.

claim: Some hypomethylation occurred proximal to TE genes.
source_text: some of the hypomethylation did occur proximal to TE genes (average of 62.1 TE genes per line)
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative result from analyzing overlap of DMRs with TE genes.

claim: The association of loss of methylation with TE gene reactivation was not clear.
source_text: The association of loss of methylation with TE gene reactivation was not clear (data not shown)
evidence_reasoning: This is based on analysis of the data that did not show a clear correlation.

claim: Very subtle depletion of DNA methylation was observed over reactivated TE genes.
source_text: however very subtle depletion of DNA methylation was observed over reactivated TE genes
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by analysis of methylation levels over reactivated TE genes.

claim: Loss of methylation may in part be responsible for reactivation of TEs.
source_text: suggesting that loss of methylation may in part be responsible for reactivation of TEs
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative inference based on the subtle depletion of methylation observed at reactivated TE genes.
